original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: Exact Pareto call-count profiles and equal-by-sign tariffs for arbitrary nonempty row/column duplications of the canonical signed 3x3 obstruction, over every nonzero unital coefficient ring.
scope_change_reason: The alphabet remains signed source/readout calls; the changed premise is the replicated rectangular demand. This answers the rectangular extension direction of PR4258 rather than adding an operation to the card alphabet.
bottleneck_link: Scoped recursive-interface side result: whole-group surcharge replaces the canonical single-operator surcharge. No physical caller or supplier saving is asserted.
stop_rule: Ship the first proved replicated-target tariff with bounded corroboration; do not extend to arbitrary rectangular targets or sign-asymmetric prices.
evidence: Written arbitrary-multiplicity proof; 30618 literal coefficient/profile cases, 2240 priced words, 46656 cover subsets, 504 dense dirty-map round trips and 672 controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact tariff with different forward/inverse prices within a duplicated group?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Individual unary and four-call optima may require incompatible common chronologies.
open_questions.first_step: Duplicate one canonical operator, give its members mixed sign preferences and seek attainable words with every other operator called twice.
open_questions.blocked_by: No common-chronology attainment theorem or matching lower bound is supplied.

open_questions.question: Which nonreplicated signed 3x4 patterns have a sharp obstruction-cover tariff?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They may contain overlapping obstructions without complete-transversal structure.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one fourth column, derive its projected lower bound and search for matching literal words.
open_questions.blocked_by: General rectangular classification and an instantiated physical caller are absent.
